data.name: Braille Translator
data.description: Use this online Braille translator to convert text to Braille or read Braille as text. It supports uncontracted Grade 1 Braille for 8 languages, Unicode cells, dot numbers and Braille ASCII, with number and capital signs, a visual dot-cell grid, and local in-browser processing.
data.description_stort: Convert text to Braille or Braille to text in your browser.
data.meta_title: Braille Translator (Text to Braille) | Ciphers Online
data.meta_description: Online Braille translator: convert English text to Braille or Braille to text. Grade 1 for 8 languages; Unicode cells, dot numbers and Braille ASCII.

data.title: How this Braille translator works
data.text:
Braille represents writing with cells of up to six raised dots arranged in two columns of three. Dots 1-2-3 run down the left column and 4-5-6 down the right, so the English letter h is dots 1-2-5. This Braille alphabet converter uses Grade 1, or uncontracted Braille: it writes each letter rather than replacing whole words with contractions.

Use it in either direction: enter ordinary text to generate Braille, or paste Braille to read it as text. When converting text to Braille, select the appropriate language for accented letters or Cyrillic. The tool supports English, Russian, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese and Turkish. Digits use the number sign (⠼), and the optional capital sign (⠠) preserves upper-case letters.

Everything runs in your browser. The converter is useful for learning the Braille alphabet, checking a short passage, or preparing a Braille-text example; it is not a live Braille interpreter, a speech service, or a replacement for proofreading material intended for embossing.

data.title: Choose a Braille format
data.text:
Choose Unicode Braille to display familiar dot cells such as ⠃⠗, dot numbers to see each cell as its raised-dot positions, or Braille ASCII for a keyboard-friendly representation. In dot-number output, cells are separated by spaces and / represents a word space. The decoder automatically recognizes Unicode cells, dot-number input and Braille ASCII.

For a Braille-to-English conversion, paste a short sample and select English if you need English letters. Because national Braille tables can assign different letters to the same cell, select the matching language whenever the source uses accented or Cyrillic characters.

data.question: What is the difference between Grade 1 and Grade 2 Braille?
data.answer: Grade 1 (uncontracted) spells words out letter by letter, usually with one cell per letter; this is what the tool produces. Grade 2 (contracted) uses contractions and short-forms, such as single cells or signs for common English words and letter groups. This Braille translator focuses on Grade 1 across its eight supported languages.

data.question: Why does the same cell decode differently in another language?
data.answer: Braille cells are reused across national writing systems: the same dot pattern can represent different accented or Cyrillic letters in different tables. Select the matching language in the settings before converting text, and select it when reading Braille from that language.

data.question: What is Braille ASCII?
data.answer: Braille ASCII maps the 64 possible six-dot Braille cells to printable ASCII characters, making Braille easier to type, copy and store in plain-text systems. This tool can create Braille ASCII and automatically recognize it when you paste it for decoding. The selected language still determines how letter cells are read.

data.question: Can I translate English to Braille and Braille to English online?
data.answer: Yes. Enter English text and use the encode direction to generate Grade 1 Braille, or paste Unicode Braille, dot numbers or Braille ASCII and use the decode direction to read it as English text. The conversion runs locally in your browser.

data.question: Which Braille input formats can I read?
data.answer: The Braille-to-text converter recognizes Unicode Braille cells, dot-number notation and Braille ASCII automatically. For dot numbers, separate cells with spaces and use / for a word space; for example, 125 is the cell for English h.

data.question: Does this Braille converter create contracted or ready-to-emboss files?
data.answer: No. It generates uncontracted Grade 1 text representations only. It does not create formatted Braille documents, control an embosser, provide certified Braille translation services, or replace a qualified proofreader for material that will be distributed or embossed.

data.question: Why does the result contain a question mark?
data.answer: A question mark means the converter could not map a character or cell in the selected Braille table. Check the chosen language, the input format and the original text. Some punctuation, symbols and characters outside the supported Grade 1 tables have no direct equivalent.

data.title: Text to Braille
data.description: Each capital gets the ⠠ sign; the rest maps letter by letter.

data.title: Dot numbers with digits
data.description: Digits follow the ⠼ number sign (3456); / marks a space.

data.title: Braille to text
data.description: Decoding restores letters and capitals from the cells.

data.title: Read Braille ASCII
data.description: The converter automatically identifies Braille ASCII; the capital sign and number sign are read with the surrounding cells.
